text.p: Most LME metals finished the day with losses but tin led the pack, falling to its weakest level in over two years. Gold and oil prices also firmed but what futures eased on indications of good global crop weather.
The CRB index was 1.6 points higher at 253.96.

LME tin slumped to the weakest level in over two years as a bearish mood gripped the market after another stocks rise. Most LME metals finished the day with losses, but copper and zinc rebounded from lows as speculative bulls showed confidence in uptrends which some analysts describe as overextended. Three months tin dived to $5,580 per tonne, the lowest since March 1995, as fund liquidation and selling gained momentum in the wake of a 400-tonne stocks rise and shaky technicals. Prices ended the day just off the lows at $5,600, a loss of $65.

"It is a lacklustre market with no bullish news whatsoever and with the stocks going up they just decided to sell it," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff. Including Thursday's build, stocks have increased so far this week by 695 tonnes after a rise of 380 tonnes last week, bringing total inventories to 12,380 tonnes. Squires said the target is now $5,500, with the next support at $5,420.

Copper held near its recent highs after a brief look at lower numbers on profit-taking sparked more speculative buying. During the morning, a stock fall of 3,550 tonnes had emboldened prices to climb to $2,537, within a whisker of Wednesday's peak. The charts indicate a correction is due, but fund and speculative buying keeps propping up the market.

"Yesterday's technical indicators did not confirm the new high so one has to watch out a bit," said Squires. The 14-day RSI has remained in overbought territory above 70 since May 15. The last time the RSI sustained a move above 70 was last November when it stayed there 11 trading days. Thursday was the 10th successive trading day copper has held above the benchmark.

Zinc showed resilience after rebounding strongly from a slide to $1,341, to end with a loss of only $3 at $1,357. It has been hovering at 4-3/4 year highs for the past several days but more tonnage showed up in the LME Singapore warehouse in Thursday's LME stocks data. Traders had been hearing for weeks that Chinese zinc was on its way into Singapore but the actual increases were enough to shake confidence. Singapore inventories recorded 3,000 tonnes of inward deliveries on Wednesday and 4,300 tonnes on Thursday. Despite the strong bounce, the market may be in for more tests of the downside, traders said. Support was pegged at $1,332 and $1,324.

Aluminium got back into a downward groove, sliding to a $1,622 low, despite a 3,700-tonne stocks drawdown. It ended down $23 at $1,622. The next important technical level is at $1,610, last Friday's low. Nickel consolidated after its recent falls, ending unchanged at $7,280, while lead closed $1 weaker at $640.

New York precious metals futures ended higher across most delivery months Thursday, with the exception of nearby platinum and palladium futures. Gold and silver prices got some support from this week's surge in platinum group metals prices due to continued disruption of Russian supplies and the brief strike at South Africa's Rustenberg mine. The dispute between the German government and Bundesbank over revaluing the latter's gold reserves was also supportive because it may make European central bank gold sales less likely, analysts said.

"Gold received some help from the PGMs via the spreads, while silver was up on some EFP buying and cash market borrowing," said Dinsa Mehta, Chase Manhattan managing director for global commodities. "But the spat between the German government and the Bundesbank, and the problem the Swiss government is also having revaluing its gold reserves, highlights the tortuous path ahead for European governments wanting to mobilize their gold reserves and may actual sales less likely," he said.

COMEX August gold, now the active contract, ended up $1.00 at $348.60 an ounce after edging up to a nine-day high of $349.20. Estimated COMEX gold volume was a high 68,000 lots. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $345.50/$346.00 against the London Thursday afternoon fix of $343.90.

NYMEX crude oil futures settled broadly higher, pulling crude products up in sympathy, after the market shrugged off stocks data in favor of bullish technical indicators, traders said. Crude oil for July delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange gained 18 cents to settle at $20.97 a barrel after rising as high as $21.28, the opening and closing price on May 13. Thursday's move up indicated a return to the market by speculative money, which had been chased out as recently as Tuesday during that session's 84-cent drop. The rally did not reflect the overall supply-and-demand fundamentals, which were seen as largely in balance, traders said.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a seasonal harvest slide amid ideas world wheat weather recently turned conducive for abundant crop production. "The general break in wheat has been due to an improvement in world weather," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man. "Since the rally, France, Australia and the U.S. have had beneficial rains." Prices closed unchanged to 8-1/2 cents a bushel lower, with July down 8-1/2 at $3.58-1/2 a bushel

CSCE world sugar futures closed firmer and just beneath session highs, but most-active July failed to rally above resistance. The contract climbed to a recent high of 11.22 cents a lb on light fund buying before settling 0.03 cent firmer at 11.21 cents a pound.
